utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. In the absence of any preliminaries, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may make quick use of this time. There were two exhibits, Your Honours, P542 and P627, which were marked for identification pending a B/C/S translation. These two have now been obtained, have been uploaded, so the Prosecution requests first that the Court Officer be given permission to attach the translations, and, second, that they finally be admitted into evidence. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. The translations now being provided, the Registry may attach the two documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the document upload in e-court. And P542 and P627 are admitted into evidence unless there were any objections. I don't think. It was just a matter of translations. And P627 is admitted under seal. Good morning to you, Mr. Van der Weijden.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday that you'll tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I wish to now turn to the main body of the report that you authored in this proceeding and the Scheduled Incidents to look at some of them in greater detail with you, although we will not have time to look at all. But, first of all, I want to ask you with respect to this type of expertise, that is, the examination of incidents to determine the origin of fire, have you ever authored any articles, reports or publications in this area of expertise that have been subjected to peer review?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to call up 65 ter number 1D00539, which is the transcript of your testimony in another proceeding, in the Perisic case, and I would like page 34 in e-court of this 65 ter number. And while we wait for that, sir, I would ask that we focus from the beginning of line 7 onwards, and if you can follow along, I will ask you to comment on the testimony from this -- this portion. "Q. I heard today, and I think you can confirmed this previously, as well, that you didn't take into account the medical reports, and you state your reasons why not, why you didn't think they would be useful or would be useful, but would you agree with me when I say this: That a medical report about certain wounds and injuries, if it contains a precise description of entry and exit wound, can fairly clearly determine the angle at which the body -- the bullet entered the body? "A. Combined with the exact location and the direction the victim was facing at the time, it would, yes. "Q. So a medical report of that kind would mean that you could establish, if you knew the position of the victim, that you would be able to establish the direction from which the bullet came; right? "A. Yes. That would be possible. "Q. And what is very important, the angle at which the bullet entered the body. "A. Yes, I understand." Now, first, I want to ask you with respect to this selection, does this accurately reflect your recollection of the testimony that you gave in the Perisic proceedings relating to this matter of the medical reports.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do not remember myself exactly what I've said at that session, but if this is the transcript, this is what I have said, and reading it now again, it's -- I still believe this is the -- still stand behind my -- my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And then if we could just continue the next section which is -- starts at line 23 in the transcript and goes on to line 3 of the next page: "Q. Did you ask the OTP to provide you with those crime reports? Did you ask them whether they had possession of any crime reports? "A. I don't remember [sic], but I don't -- I haven't received, and I haven't worked with the crime reports, and as you have stated, I'm not a -- I don't have a specific medical background, so it would be of not much use for me personally." Does this accurately represent your -- the answer you would give today on this same question?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to elaborate a little bit on that. I have medical -- I have had medical training. There are medical crime reports -- medical reports within the evidence that I received before -- that I received so -- and could have used. Only those reports were mainly focussed on the cause of death instead of technical details. But I haven't asked for additional crime reports, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What I'd like to ask you, sir, is in terms of performing your analyses and rendering your conclusions, did you have access to or did you utilize medical reports or crime reports of the nature that was discussed previously, i.e., with the entry and exit wounds delineated or described?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did use some information of the medical reports or crime reports in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall if you relied upon any descriptions of entry and exit wounds for purposes of rendering your opinions as to the Scheduled Incidents in this case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check. Just a minute. I did rely on -- in some cases, for instance, in case F1, in the -- the medical reports she was wounded on -- in a -- in her right leg, and from that -- from that information, I draw the conclusion what calibre could have been involved. In case F4, the direction of fire is based, as well -- in my beliefs on the technical and tactical possibilities but also on the information that the bullet wounded the mother in letter left thigh and wounded the daughter on her right and in her abdomen. And that's the same for F12. So there are several cases where I used medical information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in certain cases the medical information can also exclude certain calibres of munitions because they would cause greater injury and that is present in a particular victim?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't this clear from the report itself -- isn't it true that the witness has written this down in his report? I think at least twice. There's no need to repeat what is clearly in the statement or in the expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, with regards to these Scheduled Incidents that are in your report, am I correct that your analysis as to each of these incidents presupposes that the shooter was a trained sniper rather than a marksman or an ordinarily soldier with an assault rifle?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to -- I'd like to ask you with respect to these incidents, did you have information among the information provided to you by the Office of the Prosecutor that the -- that there were other witnesses who indicated that the shooters in Sarajevo were using low-power scopes and medium-quality weapons and were not persons with accuracy to be snipers?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall any information like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would such information have been relevant to your inquiry and your analysis?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I -- I nowhere in my report state that the shooter has been a sniper, so I don't see the relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, would you not agree with me in the instances where it is a long-range shot or a difficult shot that you are supposing is the source of the fire that it would therefore presuppose that the shooter was a trained shooter using a better-quality scope, for instance?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A trained shooter with better-quality scope, yes. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to show -- present you with the -- a portion of the testimony of Mr. John Jordan, a ten-year veteran of the US Marine Corps, who was also a volunteer fireman with the United Nations, who spent some considerable time in Sarajevo during the time-period that is -- that is at issue and experienced first-hand the -- what was called the sniping. And at this trial, at transcript page 1812 through 1813, line 10 onwards he states as follows, and hopefully as I read can you follow what is in today's transcript so you can -- so you can process the entirety of the statements before commenting on them: "Q. Thank you. If I can direct your attention to paragraph 24 of your statement, here is where you state and then I quote: 'I would classify most of the shooters as marksmen, not snipers.' Then later on you say most of the shooting was with medium-quality weapons with low-power scopes. Would you agree with me that here we're talking about the snipers that were shooting upon the GOFRS personnel in this paragraph? "A. I am saying that I considered most of the people who were referred to as snipers as, in actuality, gunmen, not necessarily a trained sniper who could hit somebody a thousand yards away. The expression, quote/unquote, sniper in Sarajevo was used by just about anyone to refer to when anyone was shot and when that was really not the case. Many of the people who were shot walking around were shot by men who fired a burst out of a window from a thousand yards away, and people would say the wounded person was hit by a sniper when they were actually hit by, you know, some guy literally holding a gun over a wall and letting a magazine go. They would say the person was shot by a sniper. If there were really that many good snipers there, there would have been more dead. "Q. Would the fact that these persons that were incorrectly referred to as snipers, would the fact that they were using low-power scopes, medium-quality weapons, and were not persons with accuracy to be snipers, would that mean that they would have lower accuracy than someone who would be trained as a sniper? "A. Yes." First of all, based upon your experience, would you tend to agree with the statements of Mr. Jordan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm just going to object to the -- that was a tremendous amount of testimony that was read back to the witness. If we could break down what it is he's supposed to be agreeing with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you are asked and now encouraged to split it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that, again based upon your analyses, persons tended to uses the term "sniper" even for instances where gunmen shot blindly over a wall or shot a salvo through a window?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that more or less it's the same -- the same thing that I put in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the Scheduled Incidents that you analysed, am I correct that you cannot 100 percent exclude the reasonable possibility that the scenario was caused by an untrained marksman shooting a burst through a window or letting go a salvo from an assault rifle over a wall?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, would you include a marksman shooting a burst through a door? Or through a hole in the wall? I mean, let's get concrete again. Let's get concrete. Let's see what we know about what happened and ask questions about that. I have not, apart from what Mr. Jordan gave as a possibility blindly shooting, et cetera, let's focus -- of course, you cannot exclude anything -- you cannot exclude that someone took a rifle, put it backwards over his shoulder and shot somewhere. Of course, you cannot exclude that if you had not seen the person who shot. Let's try to get to the concrete knowledge we have and see what conclusions are reasonably do be made and which ones are -- which cannot be made. Again, I, as a Judge - and I'm not speaking for my colleagues yet - I have not yet excluded someone shooting backwards, not even looking at his target. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, the -- well, the point is trying to get to the methodology of this particular witness and how he determined that a particular shot had to be an intended shot from a particular point, particularly targeting the victim who was struck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber, having read the report, is well aware of what the limitations are of what an expert can say about these things. And if you point at certain points where you say, and I think we explained that already, if I only take you back to the water level that little was known, the Chamber is fully aware that the report has to be read with a critical eye. You may proceed, and if you want to point at any matter where you think methodology is flawed, do it directly. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you briefly about optical sights and the ability to see targets through them, and to do so, I'd like to walk you through your testimony in the Perisic proceedings so, again, we need 65 ter number 1D539, and this time it will be page 39 in e-court. And, sir, if we can start at line 19 of this transcript, you can follow along, and I will have questions for you about the matters contained therein. And this will bleed over onto the -- onto the next page of the transcript: "Q. Regardless of the model, if we have an optical sight times four, do you -- would you agree with me when I say that a target which is over 600 metres -- at a distance of over 600 metres cannot be seen using those sights in view of the line in the sniper which is wider than a human face, the dividing line in the sights? "A. If the radical of the M-70 scope or M-80 scope are similar to the Soviet models or the Russian models, then, indeed, the needle which is used to target -- to put on the target is wider at larger distances like it would be for iron sights, but it doesn't mean that the bullet cannot get there. It only limits the effect of the means for the shooter to aim his rifle. "Q. At all events, if this line exists, it is an impediment to see the target at a distance greater than 600 metres; right? "A. Yes, it would." Now I want to stop there and ask you to confirm whether you still stand by what was said in the Perisic case, with the caveat that I will be also reading your further explanation from lines 10 through 25 of this page and 9 of the next page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, indeed the reticule - and it should be not "radical" but r-e-t-i-c-l-e - would cover the -- a person at the that range. However, before I train my sight on that target, the chances that the reticle will immediately cover the person without moving the scope is next to zero. So you can't exclude it, but he would have to aim his reticle at something extremely close to that target. So the chances that he hasn't seen a person in his scope are next to zero.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you to follow up on that, sir. Let's assume that the sniper or a shooter is using such a scope to target a legitimate target, a combatant, would it be possible for the reticle to mask any other items in the surrounding area such that a near miss would then strike a civilian?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the reticle of the scopes most likely used in the conflict, the -- it would only be possible if the unintended target would be below the intended target and nowhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if, for instance, you are shooting at someone on an elevation and the unintended target is farther away than the actually target, would they not, in fact, be below the intended target on the scope?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They might, if they're very close to the intended target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, if we could return to line 8 on the screen and scroll up so that the entirety of this -- through line 25 on e-court is visible. And if we could follow along: "Q. And if the magnification is in the ratio of 1:3, then at a distance of over 500 metres the same problem will occur? "A. It might, but I would like to explain something. In Western sniper courses and from the countries I know, the sniper always works with his rifle. If he works alone, he also has a pair of binoculars because you -- during my sniper course, you have a rifle with a six-time magnification, you have a pair of binoculars with six-times magnification, which has a clearer view, but you also have a spotting scope of 20-times magnification. So if I were to work alone, I had to first use the spotting scope, first use my binoculars to see moving things, things that would stand out in my field of view; then if I see things that are moving or things that stand out, I turn to my 20-times magnification to identify that object, and if it -- that were to be a target, then I put -- I use the reference that I had from my 20-times magnification, to take my rifle again to -- and use it to aim, whereas a lot of snipers, or especially in fixed positions, there could also be a spotter next to the sniper who directs -- who has bigger magnification that be the rifle scope who directs the shooter onto the target. So that's -- the three times or four times doesn't necessarily mean that it is impossible to hit the target. "Q. But would you agree with me, when the distance is greater than 1.000 metres, a sniper can have -- can be of little assistance in identifying the target? "A. I've written in my report that there were several indicators. But if you don't -- if you're not able to see the colour of the clothing but you can also see from activity of the object the way people move, people that are fighting move differently than people who are not fighting. If I'm carrying a bucket of water to my house, it looks different than when I'm trying to set up a position or carrying supplies. "Q. Yes, I read that in the report. With an optic sight, which is times four, through the sight at a distance of 1.000 metres, can you see what the target is doing, any activity, because, as far as I understand it, you can just see a dot or a point. That's what I'm asking you. Can you actually discern anything at that distance? "A. It would be possible. It would - [Microphone not activated] - but it would be possible." Now, first of all, sir, I want to ask you if you recall and if can you complete for us your answer to the last question in Perisic where your microphone was not activated. What was the full answer that you gave to the last question?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably will have said it would be possible. It would be difficult, but it would be possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And now, with that addition, does this portion of the Perisic transcript accurately reflect how you would respond to these questions today?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as part of your answer, you qualified your answer by talking of the Western sniper courses in countries that you know of when talking about the methods that might be used to overcome the visibility problems of the optical scope, and I just want to verify again now that as we discussed yesterday, you do not know what equipment was available and what training or what protocols were available for either the snipers of the Army of Republika Srpska or the snipers of the Armija, BiH, do you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my -- during my stay in -- in UNPROFOR and on the daily news, I've on several occasions seen binoculars in the hands of Serb -- Republika Srpska personnel. So there was optics available. Maybe not directly to the sniper -- to the shooters, but there were binoculars available.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. One more question about optical sights before we go to one of the incidents. Am I correct that using a scope or sight with a four-times magnification at a distance greater than 800 metres, it would be very difficult for the shooter to be able to see what a person is carrying or holding in their hands, through the scope?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be difficult to see for the -- for the shooter to see what the person is -- his actions are.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now I'd like to turn to incident F1 that you have already mentioned. So if we can turn to 65 ter number 28541. And I hope -- I hope today I have the right 65 ter number, that I haven't transposed the numbers again. And, sir, incident F1 is at page, I believe, 12 and onwards in the hard copy. Do you still have the hard copy of your report in front of you?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And this will be at page 13 and onwards in English and 16 and onwards in B/C/S for those following the e-court version. But I'd like to first ask you about the table of materials that you have at page 15 in the hard copy, page 16 in e-court in English, page 21 in the B/C/S. And, sir, I'd like to ask does this table accurately indicate the entirety of the materials that you reviewed and/or relied upon in regards to making your conclusions and performing your analysis as to this incident, the F1 incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As list -- as is listed above the table, it's the information provided by the ICTY. It doesn't mention the information that I got from my visit to the -- to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you went to visit the site, did you, in fact, review other potential shooter locations that could have resulted possibly in the type of shot that injured the victim; or did you just look at the Spicasta Stijena location to determine if it was technically possible for a bullet to have come from there?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it's not Spicasta Stijena. That's on the north-east side of Sarajevo. It is Baba Stijena. But I did say -- take into -- I visited the site, as has been my method, and looked at all possibilities, and then on te basis of my technical -- on the basis of the details, I -- I excluded on technical and tactical possibilities and determined -- tried to -- from that tried to determine where the shot might have come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in particular, for this incident, did you look at any sites that were identified to you as having been held by the BiH forces?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this incident, I didn't know where the BiH forces were. Or the VRS forces specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If -- if we look at the -- page 12 of the hard copy, page 13 in e-court, page 13, also, in the B/C/S, you identify this as being a instance of where the alleged shooting position was 920 metres from the incident site. Would you agree that this is, therefore, a long-range shot which we discussed yesterday, where you cannot exclude the possibility of a mis-shot or a ricochet?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the -- there's never -- it's never an option to exclude the possibility, but I would say in this incident that possibility is close to zero.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you would look at the photo that is on page 14 of the hard copy, and then photo 1, it's the view at the incident site from Baba Stijena. Baba Stijena, it's not a GPS co-ordinate with a 1-metre accuracy. It's the name of a big rock formation, but on that rock formation, the location that I visited, it offered a view in -- into the courtyard. And if you look around that court -- around the point of the arrow, there's no other possible target in view. There -- it's only roofs and a blind wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, unless the shooter was just wildly shooting downhill, then still the possibility that has been a random shot is extremely limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I want to ask you, you mentioned that the Baba Stijena site is not a GPS co-ordinate but is, rather, a big rock formation. How did you determine where, on that expansive formation, a shooter would have been placed, or did you pick the only position where you had a view of the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated before, I visited the incident site. From the incident site, I looked at possibilities where a shooter might have the been, and the only option that I deemed possible was on somewhere on that Baba Stijena rock from the incident site. I identified the location and then visiting Baba Stijena went to that location to take the picture that you see in photo 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct from other locations at the very same Baba Stijena you cannot have visual line of sight with the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, in order to assist the Chamber, we should be precise on that. The location you spotted, what was the size, approximately, of where you thought the bullet may have come from? Are you talking about 1 metre? Are you talking about a range of 20 metres? 10 metres? I mean, what did the definition of the location from where the bullet may have come from -- what was the size of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, Your Honour, it would be about a width of 20 metres that the shooter could have been on. I did find remnants of positions within those 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that if you would have taken the photograph from, well, let's say 5 metres away, it would still be within that range?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, sir, that at such a large or long-range distance, the trajectory of the type of rounds that you identify as being potentially used would resemble a parabola?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, as is always the case for any -- any shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correctly reading your conclusions on paragraph 6 that you would exclude the 7.62 mm round, that is an ordinary assault rifle round, because it would be inaccurate and at its extreme range to reach the target site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I would have to add it would be 7.62 times 39 millimetre since there are more rounds of calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Thank you for -- for correcting me. Let's look at 1D00513 at this time in e-court. And while we wait for that, sir, you did visit the incident site on the house at Zagrica Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the house at that street is the incident site, yes that I visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you look on the screen. Does that appear to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you refer to paragraph 6 -- conclusions on paragraph 6 that would exclude -- page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's on the middle of page 12, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just have a look. Yes. Now, let me see the question again. Yes. Your exclusion is not a factual one but is one which says this would be an unsuitable weapon to use at that distance because the accuracy would be so limited that you better use another one. Is that -- or do you exclude that a certain weapon was used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The exclusion is purely on the -- on my assumption, on my -- my beliefs that this weapon would not have the accuracy or the range for this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- incident. It's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have ignored the possibility that even a weapon which was not very suitable to hit a target at that range could, nevertheless, have been used? Although it would not be wise to use it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't ignore the possibility, but I exclude because -- there's -- of course, as mentioned before, it's not possible to exclude it, but the chances that a weapon of this kind with -- the ammunition of this kind has been used is -- it's close to zero because of the range. And the weapons from which it's fired. I haven't had the bullet in my hands, so I wouldn't be able to determine what round it was, but it's my -- it's my belief that this round hasn't been used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I was asking this question because I always want to clearly make a distinction between what actually happened, what the facts were, and what is likely to have been used as a weapon under those circumstances from such a range. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can ask you a follow-up question, sir, and if you can follow along with me. Your answer presupposes that someone with an assault rifle was intentionally targeting the -- the incident site rather than some position closer to the shooter; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I presupposed that someone with an assault rifle was --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, no, you misunderstood. Your testimony that you believe an assault rifle was not used because it's at its extreme range and would not have been accurate to target the incident site, that presupposes that the incident site is the intended target of a person who would be the shooter; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The simple question is, Mr. Van der Weijden, whether, in all your reasoning, whether you assumed that the shot was deliberately targeting the victim.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- yes, I did. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Simple questions, clear language, Mr. Ivetic, give you the best answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would an assault rifle using an ordinary 7.62 times 39 mm round be an appropriate weapon to target BiH forces located at the cemetery that is visible in your photograph on page 14? Approximately halfway between the incident site and the alleged shooter site.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see the cemetery starting there halfway up to about, I guess, three-quarters of the distance, and then an assault rifle still -- with this calibre would still not be the appropriate weapon for targeting the BiH forces. It's -- it would still be at a range over 300 metres. And firing several types of AK-47-type rifles myself, even at a range of 200 metres, it's already not an easy shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What if it's the only weapon you have?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then again as -- if I had positions on a location like Baba Stijena, I would be foolish not to request machine-guns or heavier weapons to dominate a valley below me. It's military -- from a military view it would be very unwise not to request or provide from higher up the appropriate weapons. But if --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- there was nothing available, then have you to work with what you got.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I hope we're still talking about the shooter, because I thought your report excluded the possibility of a machine-gun being used to wound this victim.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't talking about this incident. I was talking about the possibility of weapons on Baba Stijena, and I believe you asked me about the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you permit the possibility that the shooter, armed either with an assault rifle or a sniper rifle with a four times magnification, could be targeting BiH forces located in the area of the cemetery and that an errant shot or a missed shot could have struck the victim in incident F1?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to break up that question. For the assault rifle, it would be the question that I -- it would be an answer that I already elaborated on. I don't believe an assault rifle would have that range for the bullet. Even if he missed the cemetery, the -- the chances that the bullet would travel that far away and still have the -- the effect would be more than unlikely. For the sniper rifle, no. If he was targeting the cemetery, then there's no way that the -- the bullet will go out of the -- the view of the -- at least maybe not the reticle itself, but it will be in the sight, the view of the sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could this cemetery have been another possible shooting location that could have line of sight with the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as you can see by the photo that's on the -- my other screen. There's no view to anywhere above 50 metres than to Baba Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You refer to the photograph that's on the screen. Do I take it, then, that you recognise this location?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you identify this location for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken on the porch where the incident took place, and it gives a view towards -- Baba Stijena isn't exactly visible on this photograph, but I believe the -- the black markings on the photograph give a view of what the victims and the witnesses believe the shot came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that there is a line of sight from Baba Stijena visible in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there is, because it more or less resembles the photograph -- the photo that I took under different circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would move to admit this photograph into evidence as the next exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 1D513 shall be assigned Exhibit D125. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D125 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can call up 1D00515 and put that on the left side of the monitor, and 1D00516 and put it up on the right-hand side of the monitor, it might help speed things up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, looking at the left side of the monitor, the first picture, does 1D515 appear to be a different angle from the same location of that house?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. I believe it's in the vicinity because I see the porch to the right, but it's not from the same location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And from that vicinity, if you look at the right picture which is a magnification from that vicinity, do you now see the cemetery in the upper right corner as having a visual line of sight with the vicinity of the incident of sight?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you know -- strike that. Did you -- did you note the cemetery when you were doing your analysis, and did you perform any analysis in relation to positions from that location?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, my method has been to visit the exact incident site, From that incident site look where possible shooting positions were and from the exact shooting position which is above -- it is with my head on the ground since she was three years at the time she was hit in her leg. I wasn't able to see the cemetery because it was blocked out of view from the exact position, so I didn't visit the cemetery to see if I had a reverse view to the incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in order to scientifically exclude the cemetery site, one would have to go and perform the reverse of that analysis to see if there's a direct line of sight from the cemetery to the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not see -- I wasn't able to see the -- the cemetery from the exact location of the incident site, so there was no need to visit the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you were at ground level.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: A shooter would not necessarily have been aiming at the ground level, but the range might have made the bullet go lower than he was aiming; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your methodology would not have determined if a shooter had a line of sight higher than the foot of the victim; is that correct? In excluding the cemetery as a potential source for the fire.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if -- if the -- the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, a line of sight is, as I understand it, a line to be drawn from a person looking to another object. Now, to say a line of sight higher up means a different line of sight. So, therefore, a line of sight, I would way, always in that same direction I have a line of sight. Just look in the air and that's a higher up line of sight, a star, whatever, a tower. Please be --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- accurate in your questions and in the language you are using. And we are at four minutes past 10.30. Perhaps you would take your break to think about the formulation of your questions. We take a break, and -- but not before these pictures -- the 65 ter pictures where do they come from? Is it -- are they taken by whom --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They are taken by the Defence experts, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there anything known about the exact location from where the photograph was taken? And is there any information about, especially, the altitude compared to the floor of where the victim was? Because it looks -- I'm just looking at it. It -- it looks as if the position of the lens is at adult level or -- I do not know exactly. But before we draw any conclusions from all of this, I think we need to have precise information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that's why we will have our Defence witnesses to discuss that. I just wanted to see if he had seen the cemetery, and I will now be asking him after the break about -- particularly about this line-of-sight issue, because I believe there is an important point that has been missed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that may be -- we're looking forward to it. We take a break, and we resume -- but not until after the witness has left the courtroom. And we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I want to make sure that I understand the technique that you utilised to visually examine from the incident site to exclude the cemetery as a potential source of the fire. Am I correct that you, looking from ground level, that is with your head on the ground, visually with your eyes examined and could not see a straight line of sight with the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I thought you told me bullets travelled in parabolas.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you account for that?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But first when I -- in the end I ended up looking at it from ground level, but first, of course, I just took a look in the standard position, and as well we would go down. So even from the standing position I did see -- I could not see the cemetery from the exact incident site.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And how is it that you determined the exact incident site, that is to say the precise location where the victim was situated when shot?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was pointed out to me by the investigator, and it was -- as well in the -- of the witness statement of the, I believe, the mother, and there was also the exact location of where the bullet had penetrated the -- let me see, the doorsill, the doorsill. Excuse me. Sorry for the English. The wood next to the door. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The wood frame.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wood frame, sorry. So that combination determined the exact location, the level, and also the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to move to another of the incidents that you analysed, incident F3. If we can turn to 65 ter number 28541. This will be page 20 in the hard copy, page 21 in English in e-court, page 27 in B/C/S in e-court. And if we could not broadcast the same, just to be safe. I'm not sure if there's any redacted information on that one since we're using the unredacted original. And I want to ask you, when we come up with that page, does this table accurately indicate the entirety of all the source materials that you had at your disposal and which you reviewed for purposes of determining and making the conclusions that you made in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the same answer as for F1. So I believe this is the information provided by the ICTY, but it does not include my visit to the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say just as with your answer for F1, I guess I should ask you this in relation to all of the scheduled incidents. Did you actually read all of the documents that are on the table, or did you -- let's -- let's start with, first, the witness statements. Did you read all the witness statements yourself, or did you operate off of summaries that provided by the Prosecution investigators?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read, reviewed, or viewed, because there were also some photographs or video footage, but I reviewed everything that's listed in the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What about the crime reports to the extent that the crime reports are included on some of the tables? Did you review the crime reports in their entirety for the Scheduled Incidents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I did have the English translation, then I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we can turn to page 17 in the hard copy, page 18 in English in e-court, and page 23 in B/C/S in e-court. We see here that the distance from the alleged shooting site to the incident site is 1.104 metres. Would you agree, based upon our discussion, that this is a very long-range shot, as we said yesterday, subject to all of the potentials for a miss if the shooter -- because all of the factors you identified yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that this is a very long-range shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, I believe somewhere in your analysis you even said that this was at the extreme range for the type of rifle that you concluded had probably been used. Could you explain that for us? Are you saying that this rifle would not have been an appropriate rifle to use to deliberately target the -- the incident range -- the incident site? If I can help you out, it's the second-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would -- that I believe that for all weapons this is extreme range, for all small-arms. But I believe that from the weapons in the report, the rifles that I have mentioned are the most appropriate ones even though it would be at the extreme range.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it your position, then, that it would be the only logical conclusion that a rifle at its extreme range would be -- would be intentionally targeting a target that is within -- that is at its extreme range. Would that be a logical conclusion for a sniper to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could I try to analyse your question before we invite the witness to answer. Would it be the only logical conclusion that a rifle at its extreme range would be intentionally targeting a target ... I -- I -- if I don't understand the question, the answer cannot assist me, but let me just guess what I might want to ask. Is that if a rifle is used to target a target in its extreme range, that we come close to the point where the accuracy would so bad that it doesn't make much sense to use such a weapon? Is that what you intended to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For this question, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wouldn't completely agree. Quite recently I fired a rifle with the same kind of calibre that ranges up to 1.150 metres, which is at extreme range but you can still hit the target. So it's not -- it's not something you would choose, but -- well, like you said -- like I said earlier, if this is the rifle that is the most appropriate one, that's the one you would use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With -- if I understand you well, for a trained person, a fair chance of hitting the target.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you chose this potential shooting site over another one that was closer and that would not have been at its extreme range; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it also not true that the site that you identified -- so we can all follow along, let's look at page 18 in the hard copy, page 19 in English in e-court, page 25 in the B/C/S in e-court. I believe -- oops. You identified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- Mr. Ivetic, I think I -- I know where you're aiming at. Let's see whether I can put those short question to the witness and see whether that covers what you intend to find out. Looking at your report, you -- when considering the -- an origin of fire of 636 metres, you say: "The apartment block" -- That is, the block at 636 metres: "... was occupied by ABiH troops at the time, with SRK troops occupying the red-roofed apartment buildings across the street to their east. The ABiH troops would unlikely have their focus towards the canal with enemy troops that close by. In my opinion, the apartment block at 636 metres was not where the shooter was located." This seems to a very strong conclusion based exclusively on your opinion on what ABiH forces would focus at and has got little or nothing to do with the technical expertise you gave in your report. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I hope to have assisted you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You have, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, focussing again on this apartment building which was -- which would be approximately -- well, about 400-and-some metres from the alleged shooting site, did you consider that the building, apartment building held by ABiH forces could have been the target of the shooter, such that the Serb position was more logically aiming at that shot rather than a long shot at the extreme range of its weapon?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not -- I didn't consider it because it wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I may then take it that you considered it and concluded that it was not possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that it was not possible to -- for the alleged shooting position to target the apartment building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be perhaps only - let's see - the most southern corner of the apartment building, because otherwise they would be shooting their own troops through the apartment blocks where their own troops were across the street toward -- in order to hit the apartment block where the ABiH troops were. The troops were on both on the west and east side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday I believe Judge Orie already asked you about the location of the victim, so I will skip those questions. But I want to ask you: Did the information that you were provided by the Office of the Prosecutor include information that the bridge was fortified with sandbags piled 2 metres high and that there were armed ABiH soldiers near the bridge and also later on the bridge shooting in the direction of the church?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would such information, if accurate, be of importance to determining if the shots that struck the victim were intended for her or were, in fact, missed shots aimed at the ABiH soldiers, either on the -- on or around the bridge?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the ABiH soldiers would have been on the bridge and they would view the church as -- as a dangerous location, I don't think they would expose themselves on the bridge and therefore would not be visible. But if the soldiers would simultaneously with the civilian on the water's edge would be exposed, then the shots that were -- that hit the victim could be aimed at the ABiH soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could just briefly call up 1D00524. And that will be an extract from the Galic Trial Judgement. Around at paragraph 350 of the first page, the last line on the page, we see there the recitation of some of the other witnesses of this incident talking about sandbags up to a height of 2 metres being placed along the length of the bridge. And if we go on the next page, it says there: "On both sides to protect civilians closing the bridge, as well as being dug so that people would not risk being wounded or killed while fetching water from the river." At paragraph 352, we see that there were, in fact, ABiH soldiers who were near the bridge and were said to have later gone onto the -- "... positioned themselves on the bridge behind the sandbags and shot in the direction of the Orthodox church." Does this information that you did not have, is it of the type of information that would have assisted you and led you to have more detailed or different conclusions about the incident that has been labelled as F3?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would depend if I knew exactly what trail the ABiH soldiers would have been following.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, in your line of questioning, you are putting fortified positions of soldiers. And then you say shot into the direction of the Orthodox church. But -- but you then, to give a complete picture, should also read: "ABiH soldiers passing by the bridge saw what had happened." So they were not positioned at the bridge. They were passing by the bridge, and you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think I said that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I said, Your Honour, if you read my question, I said that they later positioned themselves on the bridge. I did not at all misrepresent the Judgement. I said that they were near the bridge and that they later positioned themselves on the bridge and shot at the Orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me have a look -- I'll re-read it. The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's at page 32, line 23, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I already answered the question. If I would have known exactly what the trail -- the track of the -- the troops would have been, then it might have been of use. But I do not know what their position was or exactly where they were walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I would now look to move to incident F11 briefly. That can be found beginning at -- if we return to 65 ter number 28541. This is the incident that's -- that starts at page 39 in the hard copy, page 40 in e-court in English, and page 49 in the B/C/S. And while we wait for the e-court to come up, sir, this is the incident that involved a tram line. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can turn to page 43 and 44 in the hard copy, and page 45 and 46 in the English but not broadcast the same, can you confirm, sir, that this table accurately indicates the entirety of the materials that you had at your disposal, these two pages of the table, in regards to this incident?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I believe this is the totality of the information provided by the ICTY but does not include the information that I got from visiting myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you review the medical reports listed herein?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall that the entry wound was on the thigh and the exit wound was at the hip, such that the wound canal for the named victim stretched upwards?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or downwards, depending on what side you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Or downwards, correct. Do you recall with respect to this incident that the -- during the -- during the Karadzic proceedings you viewed some videotape of this incident of other civilians that were hit near the point of the tram. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could refresh your recollection, and if we could look at 1D00536, which is the Karadzic transcript. And if we could turn to page 39 in e-court, I believe that will correlate to transcript page 7059 from that trial. And if we could look at line 17 onward, there's the video-clips that were played. And I will recite for you the question and answer that you had with respect to the video that was played from line -- I guess it's line 18: "Q. Mr. Van der Weijden, do you agree that the dust is going vertically up under a large angle, probably 90 degrees or thereabouts? "A. The particles are going up from the impact. "Q. Mr. Van der Weijden, from the Serbian positions that were 321 metres away and at the elevation of 11 [sic] metres, the descent angle in this situation could be maximum 5 degrees? "A. I did calculate that yesterday evening, and it would be just about 5 degrees."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you misspoke. I think you said 11 metres but we see in the transcript 13 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you -- with the correction of the error in my recitation, do you agree that this accurately reflects your calculations and findings of the descent angle, the maximum descent angle from the alleged shooter, the alleged Serbian position?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. It reflects the line of sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could turn to the next page in the transcript and focus on the follow-up question that was proposed at line 12: "Q. Thank you. But you can see where these people who are hit are. They are a metre away from the place where the dust is going up. What's the distance between their entry wound, which is 70 metres above the ground, and the edge of the pavement? It's approximately 90 degrees. I'm talking about angle. So, you see, they are not very far away from the pavement ... they were hit at about 70 or 80 centimetres above the ground. "Can that make a 5-degree angle or a 35- or 45-degree angle? "A. If it was just one bullet, it would not be possible. Or it would be very unlikely." Could you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, have you got one second. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's, meanwhile, proceed, but I can't have it on my screen the way I want to have it. Awaiting a solution for this, Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, this selection that I've just read, first of all, could you verify whether it's accurate and whether you would still answer the same way or hopefully explain the answer. I'm -- that's what I was really hoping you would do.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would like to explain the answer. The questions are asked in a way that it is assumed that it's only one bullet. Only in the video there is clearly a burst of fire visible with impact and several bullets hitting the area. At 321 metres, a burst from a machine-gun will, by its design, don't cover -- don't cover a group of 10 centimetres. It will be a metre or more than a metre, depending on the position of the machine-gun on a tripod, on a bipod, the experience level of the -- of the gunner. So there will always be -- the shots will never be exactly in the same location. Which I believe accounts for entry wounds centimetres above the ground and other rounds hitting the ground where the dust is visible. I would also like that -- that dust is kicked up where a bullet impacts the ground, but depending on the wind conditions of the -- of the of that day, sometimes it's not visible, sometimes it will blow straight up, sometimes it will move to the left, to the right. It depends on the wind conditions. It's just dust.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I briefly discussed it with my colleagues. It is very difficult for us to follow this evidence without having looked at the video. I hope you understand. It is all interpretation of what people have seen. We haven't seen it. Therefore, could you please find a solution such -- especially because it is about degrees and all kinds of details which I would like to be able to verify.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would hope when the -- when the Defence experts have completed their work that they will be able to come in and explain everything for you. I obviously cannot present what was presented in three days of cross-examination within the time period that we have in this case, nor do I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But the evidence is about -- you've looked at the video. This is what you see. We want to see it as well so that we are able to follow whether we agree with the observations by those who are asking questions and are giving answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I will have to move on because I don't have the video or the means to present the video at this point, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's then move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I could -- I just wanted to alert my -- counsel that I believe the video he is talking about is actually the Prosecution 65 ter 22533. I don't know what -- what portion of that video it is, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Although Ms. Stewart informs me she -- she thinks she can locate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, at least you have the assistance of the OTP if you would -- if you would go the way that enables us to look at the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In determining the -- in determining the potential location of the fire, am I correct that you excluded the buildings that were closer to the tram site and that, in fact, were looking upon the street upon which the tram travelled, which were occupied by ABiH forces?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did exclude those buildings as possible locations, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon what analyses did you exclude those locations?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On tactical assumptions. The Holiday Inn was a well-known location for the international press, and if ABiH troops would have been firing from that position onto the trams approximately 30 metres away, I don't think it would have been ignored by the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In your report at page 39 in the hard copy, which would be page 40 in e-court of 29541 -- 28541, I apologise, Your Honour. Again, I have difficulty with that number. In your discussion, you identify that the victim stated that she had heard a burst -- or had heard bursts of fire. That's under the calibre/weapons category. And I want to ask you if -- is it more likely if a shooting victim hears fire that the source of the fire is closer rather than farther away?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an urban environment, with echoing of buildings, the source of fire would be -- would have to be over 600 metres to -- to lessen the sound. 300 metres away is clearly hearable.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to call up 65 ter number 1D00423. This is an information report from the interview of General Sir Michael Rose with the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal. And if we could turn to page 3 of the document, this is a selection I'd like to present to you and ask some questions about. And it begins by saying -- it's at the bottom of the page in English so we can follow along: "I am sure that the Serbs were firing at the trams, but I believe Ganic also organised his secret police to snipe trams. His sniper unit sniped so that the angle of the shot matched the direction of the [sic] Serb line. During long cease-fires, I think that Ganic and the Muslims were responsible for breaking the cease-fire. This kept the tension." Sir, in performing your analysis, did the Prosecution provide information to you or was it otherwise available that the Bosnian Presidency secret police snipers were believed to be sniping at the trams in a way to mimic the angle and -- to mimic the direction of the Serb line?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is part of the evidence, and I've read all the evidence. I believe this is part of the -- I -- I have read this. I have taken into account, because I tried to identify all possible shooting locations, if -- if shooters would try to mimic Serb forces on -- across the river, in -- in their angle of fire they would have to lean out of windows in order to be able to hit from -- to hit the trams travelling when they passed the intersections. So, therefore, leaning out of windows with the enemy -- in clear view of the enemy, in my view, would be -- well, tactically very unwise and very dangerous. So I don't believe, in this case, that it could have been done from another position, although I don't know exactly who was in the building across -- across the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to be clear, you said you believe you've read this part. Is it your testimony that you have read this information sheet previously or that you've -- or were made aware of its contents? Which -- which is it?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember there are -- this is the list of the -- of the information that I was provided at this time. I -- I do recall information about this. I -- I can't remember exactly where, but I've -- it is familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. I would like to move along to more one incident before our time is up. F9, which begins at page 34 in your hard copy, page 35 in the English version in e-court, and page 43 in the B/C/S. And if we could not broadcast the same, that way we could be assured that I'm not broadcasting any sensitive information. And ... and, here, you have noted that the -- that uniformed soldiers warned the victim of an active sniper. Am I correct and was it your understanding that these soldiers were Armija BiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were uniformed soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would you permit that uniformed soldiers would have been an appropriate and legitimate target for the opposing side to shoot at?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the uniformed soldiers would have been in the same view of -- the same side picture for the shooter, then they -- well, I would agree that a uniformed soldier could present a legitimate target.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did the information you received from the Office of the Prosecutor, in relation to this incident, include any information as to the placement of BiH or -- or Armija BiH personnel in the vicinity of the incident site?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say 100 per cent that I'm sure exactly where the -- those uniformed soldiers were at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did the information given to you by the Office of the Prosecutor in relation to this event identify how far this location was from the confrontation or front line?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only -- the -- the trench that is mentioned in the reports is a trench to -- to cross a street safely. It doesn't mention where exactly the front line was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If we turn to page 36 of your hard copy, and page 37 in English in e-court, and page 45 in the B/C/S in e-court. And -- perhaps I should repeat that. So page 37 in English in e-court and page 45 in the B/C/S. And we have here a photograph that you say was part of the information given to you by the ICTY to enable you to write the report. Can I take it that you did not actually go to the site yourself to take a photograph from the alleged shooting site. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have the wrong page in B/C/S on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It should be the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell me why it was that you did not go to the incident site to verify that the information provided to you by the Office of the Prosecutor was, in fact, accurate?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did visit the incident site. I didn't go to the alleged shooting position. There was no possibility to visit the shooting location at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also, the -- there used to be holes in the blind side, and the picture that I was provided by the ICTY was taken from one of those holes, former windows, but since the -- on the blind side those holes had been fixed, there was no need for me to go there, as well as that there was such a wide view of the -- of the area that I didn't deem it necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The photographs appears to have a magnification of -- of the site. Do you happen to know what magnification or zoom factor was being used for this photograph?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You state in your report that this was taken in the upper level of the school of the blind. Can you be more precise? What floor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The upper level. There's -- for the building, there are two -- in English, I believe, first floor is the ground floor. So it would be on the second floor. Or higher. And on -- on the attic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that there are other positions from which the bullet could have come from that could have produced the same injuries?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have come from the windows in the -- on the -- the southeastern side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the windows on the same building or a different building?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are other possibilities where the bullet might have come from, but since the girls were using the buildings to -- to walk, it would have been strange for the shooter to wait if he had been in the -- in the -- in one of the buildings that encircles the -- the square where the girls were, to wait until she was at the corner. At the end of the trench.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did the information provided to you also indicate where Dobrinja was located? That -- the road towards Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK VAN DER WEIJDEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember that, looking at the map, that I was aware where Dobrinja was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up 1D527 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, before doing so and perhaps it could be done. Could I ask the witness one clarifying question. I think it's not only at this incident that you draw conclusions from when the shooter fired. Now, if I am in a position where I can see the victim, well, let's say, walking for a hundred metres, a nearby position, and if there is a position further away where you can see the person moving only for 5 or 7 metres, because that's, I think, the situation we are comparing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you say, I would not have expected the shooter to wait that long. And this is not the only incident where you draw such a conclusion. Now, if someone, if I see someone walking from a nearby position for 50 metres, you could also say, Take your time. If that person is exactly in the middle, or I take my time to see whether there are no other possible victims, or whatever, I mean, what is it in your professional experience or expertise that you would expect a shooter always to engage the target not halfway but right in the beginning, and you draw quite some conclusions on the basis of that. Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could, Your Honour. If I'm in a prone position, that is, a position lying on the ground behind my weapon, which is the position that is the most stable, and for a longer time is the most preferred position by most shooters. The other position would be on a table, on a chair behind a table with a sandbag on the table which is in the sport shooting world knows as benchrest shooting, those are the two most stable positions. The problem with those positions that -- with being in a position like that is you can -- you have only a small arc in which you can use your weapon. So if the target is outside of that arc, you would have to shift your position, aim again, and then eventually it's only a couple of metres that you are -- you are at your utmost -- most comfortable position. So if I wait for a long time, so at 50 metres and the victim would move 400 metres, I would have to change position probably more than ten times, which is not something that I would do. I would -- if there's a moving target in this case, as she would have been if she was fired at from within that square, I would have to -- I would spot her, I would shift my position before her, that -- that she's walking into my arc of fire, and then wait until she's in, follow her, and then put my sights slightly before her, and then wait until she walked into my sights, and then I would fire. I so hope it explains why I excluded -- it depends -- it's about shooting from a good position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, it seems that the whole of your answer is based on having the target within the arc already right at the beginning. Now I am in a comfortable position as a shooter. I see someone. I'm nearby. I have a long range. I know that that person is moving in such a direction that in five seconds or ten seconds will enter the arc of where I am positioned now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you could also say instead of moving, which you say is not easy, not very comfortable. Let's just wait until the person is there. I'll then aim, pull the trigger, I don't have to move my weapon at all. So, therefore, that would be a logical explanation for not shooting immediately when the person comes in sight. I'm trying to understand your -- your logic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. The -- I agree that I would -- I could wait a few seconds, but the longer a target is visible, I don't know exactly what the target will do. So if the target -- if there's a wall or a door and the target will disappear, then I will have missed my shot, so ...
